obligations.note: In service.py, LedgerService.amend_memo used to call self._audit(actor, "amend_memo", ...) and now only writes an app log line. The memo edit is still saved (payments.amend_memo calls store.set_payment_memo), so a state-changing operation now has no audit event. The sample-only AUD-1 control test checks create, approve and release only, so it can't catch this.
Ticket CHG-24556 is standard, approved by change manager Grace Kim on 2026-10-17, before the PR opened on 2026-10-19. Its components (payments.service) cover the only touched path, service.py.
The code_review approval is from mara.costa@fernbrook.example, a payments change_approver who is a different person from the author Sofia Santos (checked against all directory aliases).
The approval names head commit c4ac273, the only commit in the change, so no later commits exist.

records/ci/run.json shows the full payments suite passing on head c4ac273: 172 tests, 0 failures, 0 skipped. That includes the registered AUD-1 control test test_sampled_operations_are_audited, which is labelled sample and doesn't exercise amend_memo.
The only touched file is service.py (component payments.service, security_sensitive false), so no security review is required.
No protected paths are touched: no controls data, control tests or CI files are in the diff.
The ticket type is standard and the change is not marked emergency, so no post-implementation review is required.
No exception in the register covers AUD-1 for payments.service. The deviation from AUD-1 is therefore not covered by any approved exception.
No acceptance-ledger entry covers service.py, so no earlier evidence lapses because of this change.

summary: The change swaps the audit call in LedgerService.amend_memo for an application log line, so memo edits, which still change saved payment data, no longer record an audit event. That breaks AUD-1, and no exception covers it. CI is green only because the sample-based AUD-1 control test never edits a memo, and the change description doesn't mention dropping the audit. The ticket, independent review and approval of the final commit are all in order, but the AUD-1 violation alone requires rejection.
